audience_description: A SaaS founder, growth marketer, or product strategist who is considering a major repositioning from services/agency to self-serve SaaS, and wants to understand how Foreplay executed this transition — specifically how they signaled the shift to their existing audience without losing credibility.
recommended_h1_format: How [Company] Pivoted from Agency to SaaS: A 5-Year Homepage Teardown
secondary_keywords: Foreplay CRO teardown agency to SaaS
how Foreplay repositioned as SaaS platform
Foreplay homepage evolution D2C to software
Foreplay winning ad workflow messaging strategy
content_angle: Lead with the STRATEGIC RISK of the pivot — going from 'we do the work for you' to 'you do it with our software' is a positioning death trap for most agencies. Show how Foreplay used their homepage to reframe proof of work (portfolio → product features), rebuild trust (founder voice → system authority), and justify the higher perceived price (bespoke service → category ownership). The searcher isn't interested in design criticism; they want to know: 'Did this risky move work, and what were the signal decisions that made it work?'
what_the_searcher_wants: Patterns and decision logic they can apply to their own services-to-SaaS transition — specifically how to migrate an audience from 'hiring us' to 'using our software' without looking like you abandoned them.
what_to_avoid: Treating this as a simple design refresh or describing the changes as surface-level. The searcher will see through generic 'we added a product nav and changed the headline' analysis. Avoid missing the fundamental repositioning logic: Foreplay removed 'Hire Us' and replaced it with 'Start Free Trial' — that's not a CTA change, it's a business model change. Also avoid crediting the shift to aesthetics alone; the real story is that they moved from selling expertise to selling a system, which required completely different messaging architecture.
